title: The effects of different designs of indoor biophilic greening on psychological and physiological responses and cognitive performance of office workers
research_question: To investigate the effects of different biophilic designs (Japanese, tropical) in office rooms on the psychological and physiological responses and cognitive performance of office workers, compared to a green-free control design.

participants.description: 18 healthy office workers (mean age: 33.4 ± 11.3 years, 14 women, 13 men) without neurological disorders. (27 initially recruited, 9 excluded due to data issues).

stimuli_or_exposures.description: An office room (3.0m L x 4.0m W x 2.2m H) with three designs: 1) Japanese biophilic design (indigenous Japanese/East Asian plants), 2) Tropical biophilic design (tropical plants), 3) Control (green-free). Green visibility was 0.30 for Japanese and 0.31 for Tropical. Environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, illuminance) were similar across conditions.

measures.instrument: Heart rate variability (HRV) (lnLF, lnHF, LF/HF, HR)
Electroencephalography (EEG) (absolute and relative power for theta, alpha 1, alpha 2, beta 1, beta 2 bands) across 5 ROIs
Semantic Differential Method (SDM) (10 adjective pairs, 7-point Likert scale)
Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS) Japanese edition (16 moods, 6-point Likert scale)
Stroop color and word task (accuracy rate, reaction time)

mechanisms: Attention Restoration Theory (ART): Exposure to nature can replenish attentional resources and reduce directed attention fatigue.
Stress Recovery Theory (SRT): Exposure to nature increases positive affect and facilitates recovery from physiological stress.

Neural efficiency hypothesis: Higher neural activation for equivalent performance indicates less efficient neural processing. Greening designs lead to lower beta 2 power, suggesting reduced hyper-alertness/anxiety and more efficient neural processing during cognitive tasks.
implementation_implications: Indoor greening, particularly with Japanese designs, can improve the office environment by decreasing negative emotions and promoting a sense of calm and comfort.
Biophilic designs can enhance neural efficiency during cognitive tasks, even if behavioral performance is not overtly improved.

Different biophilic designs (e.g., Japanese vs. tropical) can elicit distinct emotional responses, suggesting the need for design specificity based on desired psychological outcomes (e.g., Japanese for calming, tropical for positive mood states).

limitations: The study did not find behavioral performance differences in cognitive tasks, contrasting with some previous studies.

Participants' awareness of the research purpose due to informed consent instructions might have unconsciously affected subjective and behavioral indicators. A blinded study design is recommended for future research.

paper_metadata.title: The effects of different designs of indoor biophilic greening on psychological and physiological responses and cognitive performance of office workers
paper_metadata.crossref_title: The effects of different designs of indoor biophilic greening on psychological and physiological responses and cognitive performance of office workers
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Impression on biophilic designs influences the effects of indoor greening. The current study aimed to investigate the effects of different biophilic designs in office rooms on the psychological and physiological responses and the cognitive performance of office workers. Indoor greening rooms with Japanese and tropical designs were used along with the green-free (control) design in this study. The heart rate variability of the participants was not affected by green designs. However, there was improvement in impressions on tropical and Japanese designs in office rooms. In particular, the Japanese design was more effective in decreasing negative emotions than the tropical design. The electroencephalography during 5-min exposure to the greening designs showed limited frequency bands and regions of interest affected by the greenery design. Taken together with the psychological data, indoor greening with the tropical design promoted positive mood states. Meanwhile, indoor greening in the Japanese design, inhibited negative mood states. However, there were no significant differences between the two designs in terms of cognitive task performance. Hence, indoor greening increases neural efficiency during cognitive tasks.
